tracks.title: The Stardust Engine (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: Like the rest of *Electric Color*, *"The Stardust Engine"* was officially released in 1987 (buried by Apex Records at the very end of the album as Track 13). In truth, it was the very first song Cassidy and Ryan O'Connell came up with in 1986 when their twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright joined them at CPI in Blacksburg. Too scared at the time to shop the song around, the four of them kept it to themselves and decided to use that first song to name their band: **The Stardust Engine**. Twenty-five years later, the band's eponymous theme is reborn as the opening calibration sequence of 2011's *Starfield Calibration*—stripped of Apex Records' 1987 neon gloss and rebuilt from the ground up inside Cassidy O'Connell's proprietary **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** (an in-universe trademark of Engine Room Records, LLC; not registered in real life), suspending Ryan and Cassidy's sibling duet inside a 360-degree zero-gravity planetarium dome.

tracks.title: Electric Color (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: In 1987, *"Electric Color"* was the band's Trojan horse—a blindingly bright synth-pop hit engineered to satisfy Apex Records' radio quotas while concealing lyrics about dissociation and creative captivity. Twenty-four years later, Cassidy O'Connell reclaims the song completely on solo vocals, replacing the brittle 1980s studio brass with warm, zero-gravity Oberheim pads and a hypnotic fretless bassline by Evan Wright. In the Cosmic Tidal Lock mix, the "neon lights" are no longer fluorescent studio cages—they are deep-space auroras.

tracks.title: Worlds Apart (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: On 1987's *Electric Color*, *"Worlds Apart"* was marketed by Apex Records as a conventional separation ballad, though Ironheads quickly decoded its true meaning: the agonizing distance between Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell when industry handlers tried to divide them in the studio. Re-engineered in **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™**, the song's "silent satellite" metaphor becomes literal—two voices separated across the vacuum of space, locking onto the same frequency across a million miles of static.

tracks.title: Rearview Mirror (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: On 1987's *Electric Color*, *"Rearview Mirror"* was Cassidy's quiet lament about feeling like a passenger in her own career (*"I'm just a passenger in this ride / With all this 'Stardust' left inside"*), as Apex Records reduced her and Ryan's love of the cosmos and rockets into a cheap corporate naming gimmick. Looking back twenty-four years later on 2011's *Starfield Calibration* from the helm of her own zero-gravity sanctuary, Cassidy flips the 1987 lyric on its head: *"I used to be a passenger on their ride / With all this Stardust locked inside / Now I'm at the helm of the frequency / And the whole horizon belongs to me!"*

tracks.title: Atmosphere (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: Originally recorded in September 1992 for the canceled *Friction* album (where rogue Apex executive Julian Vance infamously misinterpreted its literal space-shuttle re-entry physics—*"Here comes the friction, feel the fire"*—as sexual innuendo), *"Atmosphere"* existed for nineteen years only as an early rough cut (*"Atmosphere (1992 Demo)"* on the 1996 *Ad Astra* single and *"Atmosphere (Warehouse Demo)"* on 2007's *Lost Sounds*). Because that 1992 rough demo sounded like an early-1990s track tracked under label pressure, the band was never happy with it. On 2011's *Starfield Calibration*, Cassidy and Ryan finally deliver the **definitive, finalized version** of *"Atmosphere"*—using **The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™** to bring the song back to the lush, shimmering 1980s sound they love so much.

tracks.title: Echoes in the Wire (Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix)
tracks.loreNote: Originally introduced on 1997's *Hard Reset* to permanently replace 1989's *"If You Walked Away"*—a forced Apex Records breakup ballad whose abandonment scenario caused Cassidy (who is autistic) severe backstage distress after every concert, requiring her brother and safe person Ryan to hold her tightly in twenty-minute deep-pressure grounding hugs. *"Echoes in the Wire"* is the story of Cassidy finding comfort, quiet, and safety when Ryan is hugging her tightly as the stage noise fades away (*"All the terrestrial static faded out / Leaving nothing of the doubt... We traded time for something real / A tidal lock that you can feel"*). In this 2011 **Cosmic Tidal Lock Mix**, Cassidy wraps that grounding embrace in warm, zero-gravity analog synthesizer pads and a soothing 96 BPM heartbeat.
